findings.description: The bucket is created with no ACL restriction, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access; the inline comment confirms the bucket is intended to be public. It stores a customer master data object, so anonymous users could read sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so access to a publicly reachable bucket holding customer data leaves no audit trail for detecting unauthorised reads.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects overwritten or deleted (including by an attacker with write access to this public bucket) cannot be recovered.
A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which has no public access block or encryption, exposing sensitive customer records to unauthenticated retrieval.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced KMS encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, leaving no audit record of object access for forensic or compliance purposes.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so deletion or tampering with financial objects is irreversible.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could make it public without any account-level guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data is stored unencrypted with no customer-managed key control.
No logging block is configured, so there is no audit trail of read or write access to this bucket.
The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so account or bucket-level public access is not explicitly denied.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving stored datasets unencrypted with no enforced KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so nothing prevents a subsequent ACL or policy change from exposing the bucket publicly.

The central log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; it uses the log-delivery-write canned ACL, and without an explicit public access block a policy change could expose aggregated access logs.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The log bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or deletion of audit logs would not be recorded.
None of the buckets, including the log bucket, attach a bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so data may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
